name: Algebra II
description: Advanced algebra extending into functions, polynomials, rational expressions, exponential and logarithmic functions, sequences, series, probability, and conic sections.

modules.title: Review: Linear & Quadratic Functions
modules.objectives: Graph linear and quadratic functions; convert to vertex form; calculate the discriminant; solve real-world quadratic problems. Students will show step-by-step reasoning, check solutions for accuracy, and apply the method to the module assignment or a real problem.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.1 — quadratic form, graphs, vertices, and applications.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video — Module 1: Review: Linear & Quadratic Functions.
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Complete this provided set. Graph vertex-form functions y=(x−2)²−3, y=−2(x+1)²+4, y=0.5(x−4)², y=3(x+2)²−1, and y=−(x−3)²+5; graph standard-form functions y=x²−6x+5, y=−x²−4x+5, y=2x²+8x+6, y=0.5x²−2x−2, and y=−3x²+12x−9. For each, identify vertex, axis of symmetry, opening, and discriminant. Then model a ball launched from 5 ft with h(t)=−16t²+32t+5: find its maximum height, physically meaningful domain, and landing time. Submit: one numbered PDF or clear scan with ten labeled graphs and the model solution. Include: axes, vertices, symmetry lines, discriminant work, algebra, units, domain, and a substitution check. Evaluation: correct representations, complete reasoning, accurate notation, readable graphs, and verification.

modules.title: Polynomial Functions
modules.objectives: Describe end behavior using leading coefficients; find zeros and their multiplicities; apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; sketch polynomial graphs.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.3 — zeros, multiplicity, end behavior, and polynomial graphs.
modules.videoNote: GIIS lesson video — Module 2: Polynomial Functions.
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Analyze these six polynomial functions: f(x)=(x−2)²(x+1), g(x)=−(x+3)(x−1)², h(x)=x(x−2)(x+2), p(x)=(x−1)³(x+2), q(x)=2(x+1)²(x²+1), and r(x)=−(x−2)(x+1)(x²+4). For each, state degree and leading term, determine end behavior, list all real zeros with multiplicities, state the number of remaining nonreal complex zeros, and sketch the graph. Verify with the free Desmos web graphing calculator at https://www.desmos.com/calculator or with a hand-generated value table if that site is unavailable. Submit: one numbered PDF or clear scan containing six analyses and graphs. Include: algebraic reasoning, verification method, and any mismatch you corrected. Evaluation: accurate graph features, justified multiplicities, readable graphs, and agreement.

Use synthetic division for (x³+4x²−7x−10)÷(x−2), (2x⁴−3x³+5x−1)÷(x+1), (x⁴−5x²+4)÷(x−1), (3x³−2x²+x−6)÷(x−2), and (x⁵+2x⁴−x+3)÷(x+2). Multiply or divide these pairs: [(x²−4)/(x²+x−6)]·[(x−2)/(x+2)], [(x²−9)/(x²−1)]÷[(x−3)/(x−1)], [(2x)/(x²−4)]·[(x+2)/(3x)], and [(x²−1)/(x²+2x+1)]÷[(x−1)/(x+1)]. questions.question: Which of the following is the vertex form of a quadratic function?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is y = a(x − h)² + k, where (h, k) is the vertex of the parabola.

questions.question: What is the vertex of f(x) = 2(x − 3)² + 5?
questions.explanation: In vertex form y = a(x − h)² + k, the vertex is (h, k). Here h = 3 and k = 5, so vertex is (3, 5).

questions.question: Describe the end behavior of f(x) = −2x³ + x − 4.
options: As x → ∞, f → ∞ and as x → −∞, f → −∞
As x → ∞, f → −∞ and as x → −∞, f → ∞
questions.answer: As x → ∞, f → −∞ and as x → −∞, f → ∞
questions.explanation: Leading term is −2x³. Odd degree with negative leading coefficient: falls right, rises left.

questions.question: Divide (x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6) by (x − 3) using synthetic division. What is the quotient?
questions.explanation: Synthetic division with root 3 gives coefficients 1, 1, and −2 with remainder 0.

questions.question: Simplify the rational expression: (x² − 4) / (x² − x − 2). State the simplified expression on its original domain.
questions.explanation: Factor numerator: (x+2)(x−2). Factor denominator: (x−2)(x+1). Cancel (x−2). Result: (x+2)/(x+1). The original denominator is zero at x=2 and x=−1, so both exclusions remain.

questions.question: For real variables x and y, simplify ∛(x⁶y³).
questions.explanation: ∛(x⁶y³) = x^(6/3) · y^(3/3) = x²y. Dividing each exponent by 3 works because both radicand exponents are multiples of the cube-root index.

questions.question: A population triples every 4 years. Starting at 500, which function models the population after t years?
questions.explanation: Every 4 years the population is multiplied by 3. The growth factor 3 is raised to the power t/4.

questions.question: Using the definition of a logarithm, evaluate log₂(64).
questions.explanation: Since 2⁶ = 64, log₂(64) = 6. This is the exponent to which the base 2 must be raised, so the value is 6 rather than the base or the result.

questions.question: Which property of logarithms is used to expand log(ab)?
questions.explanation: The Product Rule states log(ab) = log(a) + log(b). It converts a logarithm of a product into a sum of logarithms; the Quotient and Power Rules have different forms.

questions.question: Rewrite the equation in exponential form and solve log₃(x) = 4.
questions.explanation: log₃(x) = 4 means 3⁴ = x. 3⁴ = 81. The exponential form also confirms x is positive, which is required for the logarithm’s argument.

questions.question: Solve (x + 2)/(x − 1) = 3 and respect the original domain restriction.
questions.explanation: Cross multiply: x + 2 = 3(x − 1) = 3x − 3. So −2x = −5; x = 5/2. The result is allowed because 5/2 does not make the original denominator x−1 equal zero.

questions.question: Which equation has a vertical asymptote at x = 2?
questions.explanation: A vertical asymptote occurs where the denominator is zero and the factor does not cancel. Here x − 2 = 0 at x = 2.

questions.question: Solve √(2x + 3) = 5 and check the result in the original equation.
questions.explanation: Square both sides: 2x + 3 = 25. 2x = 22; x = 11. Check: √(22 + 3) = √25 = 5. ✓.

questions.question: Explain the relationship between exponential functions and logarithmic functions. Give one example of each and show they are inverses of each other.
questions.answer: A complete response should answer this prompt directly: Logarithmic functions are the inverses of exponential functions. For example, f(x) = 2^x and g(x) = log₂(x) are inverses because f(g(x)) = 2^(log₂x) = x and g(f(x)) = log₂(2^x) = x.
questions.explanation: The inverse relationship means their graphs are reflections across y = x, and composing them returns the original input.

questions.question: $1,200 is invested at an annual interest rate of 5%, compounded quarterly. Write the formula and compute the value after 3 years (round to the nearest cent).
questions.answer: A complete response should answer this prompt directly: A = 1200(1 + 0.05/4)^(12) ≈ $1,392.91.
questions.explanation: Substitute P = 1200, r = 0.05, n = 4, and t = 3 into A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), then round only the final value to the nearest cent.

questions.question: For 3x² − 4x + 2 = 0, what is the discriminant and what does it show about real solutions?
questions.explanation: Using b² − 4ac gives (−4)² − 4(3)(2) = 16 − 24 = −8. A negative discriminant means there are no real roots.

questions.question: A polynomial p(x) has zeros at x = −2 (multiplicity 2) and x = 3 (multiplicity 1). Which describes its graph?
options: Touches the x-axis at −2, crosses at 3
Crosses the x-axis at −2, touches at 3
Touches the x-axis at both −2 and 3
questions.answer: Touches the x-axis at −2, crosses at 3
questions.explanation: Even multiplicity → graph touches (bounces). Odd multiplicity → graph crosses. x = −2 has multiplicity 2 (even), x = 3 has multiplicity 1 (odd).

questions.question: Use the Factor Theorem: Is (x + 2) a factor of p(x) = x³ − x² − 4x + 4?
Which is a correct simplification of (x² − 9)/(x² + 6x + 9)?
questions.explanation: Numerator: (x+3)(x−3). Denominator: (x+3)². Cancel one (x+3): (x−3)/(x+3). The original expression still excludes x=−3, even though the common factor cancels during simplification.

questions.question: Solve √(x − 1) = x − 3 and reject any extraneous solution.
questions.explanation: Squaring gives x = 2 or x = 5, but x = 2 makes the right side negative and is extraneous.

questions.question: Convert 16^(3/4) to simplest radical form.
questions.explanation: Because 16=2⁴, 16^(3/4)=(2⁴)^(3/4)=2³=8. Equivalently, take the fourth root first and then cube the result.

questions.question: A radioactive substance decays according to A(t) = 200e^(−0.035t). What is the half-life (to the nearest year)?
Condense: 2log(x) + log(y) − log(z). Assume x>0, y>0, and z>0.
questions.explanation: Power rule: 2log(x) = log(x²). Product rule: log(x²) + log(y) = log(x²y). Quotient rule: log(x²y) − log(z) = log(x²y/z). The positivity assumptions keep all real logarithms defined.

questions.question: Express both sides with the same base and solve 5^(2x) = 125.
questions.explanation: Because 125 = 5³, the exponents must match: 2x = 3, so x = 3/2. Substitution checks the result: 5^(2·3/2)=5³=125.

questions.question: Find the 8th term of the arithmetic sequence: 3, 7, 11, 15, …
questions.explanation: a₁ = 3, d = 4. aₙ = 3 + (n−1)·4. a₈ = 3 + 7·4 = 3 + 28 = 31. Each term increases by 4, so the explicit rule and the listed pattern agree.

questions.question: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + …
The standard form equation of an ellipse with center at the origin, horizontal major axis of length 10, and minor axis of length 6 is:
questions.explanation: Semi-major axis a = 5 (horizontal), semi-minor axis b = 3. Standard form: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 = x²/25 + y²/9 = 1.

questions.question: A class of 15 students must elect a president, vice-president, and treasurer (no person can hold two offices). How many ways can this be done?
questions.explanation: The three offices are distinct, so order matters: 15 choices for president, 14 for vice-president, and 13 for treasurer give 15×14×13=2730.

questions.question: A data set has mean 70 and standard deviation 5. What z-score corresponds to a value of 82?
questions.explanation: z = (x − μ)/σ = (82 − 70)/5 = 12/5 = 2.4. The positive sign places 82 above the mean, and 2.4 is the distance measured in standard deviations.

questions.question: For A=[[2,1],[1,4]] and B=[[3,0],[−1,2]], what is the (1,1) entry of AB?
questions.explanation: Use the first row of A and the first column of B: 2·3+1·(−1)=5. This row-by-column rule determines each entry of a matrix product and preserves the required order of factors.

questions.question: Which system of inequalities has the feasible region in the first quadrant bounded by y ≤ 4 and x + y ≤ 6?
questions.explanation: First quadrant requires x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0. Adding y ≤ 4 and x + y ≤ 6 creates the bounded feasible region.

questions.question: Solve the system: x + y + z = 6, 2x − y + z = 3, and x + 2y − z = 2.
questions.explanation: Substituting (1, 2, 3) satisfies all three equations: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6, 2 − 2 + 3 = 3, and 1 + 4 − 3 = 2.

questions.question: A substance has a pH of 3.5. Given pH = −log[H⁺], find the hydrogen ion concentration [H⁺] in scientific notation. What does this pH value indicate about the substance?
questions.answer: A complete response should answer this prompt directly: [H⁺] = 10^(−3.5) ≈ 3.16 × 10⁻⁴ mol/L. The substance is acidic (pH < 7). A strong response should use Algebra II final concepts vocabulary, answer the full prompt, and include reasoning or evidence rather than a one-word reply.
questions.explanation: pH = −log[H⁺] → log[H⁺] = −3.5 → [H⁺] = 10^(−3.5) ≈ 3.16 × 10⁻⁴. pH < 7 indicates an acid.

questions.question: A ball is launched upward from a cliff 80 ft high with initial velocity 64 ft/s. Its height is h(t) = −16t² + 64t + 80. Find the maximum height and the time at which it is reached.
questions.answer: A complete response should answer this prompt directly: Maximum height is 144 ft at t = 2 seconds. A strong response should use Algebra II final concepts vocabulary, answer the full prompt, and include reasoning or evidence rather than a one-word reply.

questions.question: A student earns scores of 72, 85, 90, 68, and 95 on five tests. Calculate the mean and population standard deviation. Would a score of 60 be considered unusual? Explain using z-scores.
questions.answer: A complete response should answer this prompt directly: Mean = (72+85+90+68+95)/5 = 82. Population σ ≈ √[(100+9+64+196+169)/5] = √[538/5] ≈ √107.6 ≈ 10.37. z for 60 = (60−82)/10.37 ≈ −2.12. Since |z| > 2, a score of 60 is considered unusual.
questions.explanation: Using the five scores as the full population, a z-score beyond ±2 is generally considered unusual under the stated classroom convention.

quizQuestions.question: What is the axis of symmetry of f(x) = x² − 6x + 8?
quizQuestions.explanation: Axis of symmetry: x = −b/(2a) = −(−6)/(2·1) = 3. This vertical line passes through the vertex and splits the parabola into mirror-image halves.

quizQuestions.question: A quadratic opens downward when:
quizQuestions.explanation: When the leading coefficient a is negative, the parabola opens downward. The sign of b shifts the graph but does not determine whether its arms point upward or downward.

quizQuestions.question: The discriminant of x² − 4x + 4 = 0 is:
quizQuestions.explanation: b² − 4ac = 16 − 4(1)(4) = 16 − 16 = 0. One repeated real root. A zero discriminant means the quadratic has one real solution counted twice.

quizQuestions.question: For f(x)=−2(x+1)²+7, which statement is true?
options: The vertex is (−1, 7) and the graph opens downward
The vertex is (1, 7) and the graph opens upward
The axis is x=7 and the graph opens downward
The vertex is (−1, −7) and the graph opens upward
quizQuestions.answer: The vertex is (−1, 7) and the graph opens downward
quizQuestions.explanation: Vertex form a(x−h)²+k gives h=−1 and k=7; because a=−2, the parabola opens downward.

quizQuestions.question: For h(t)=−16t²+32t+5, what is the initial height h(0)?
quizQuestions.explanation: Substituting t=0 gives h(0)=5, so the object starts 5 feet above the reference level.

quizQuestions.question: The end behavior of f(x) = 4x⁵ − x is:
quizQuestions.explanation: Degree 5 (odd) with positive leading coefficient: falls left (x→−∞) and rises right (x→∞).

quizQuestions.question: How many zeros (counting multiplicity) does a degree-4 polynomial have?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra states a degree-n polynomial has exactly n zeros (counting multiplicity, including complex zeros).

quizQuestions.question: A zero with even multiplicity means the graph:
options: Touches and bounces at the x-axis
quizQuestions.answer: Touches and bounces at the x-axis
quizQuestions.explanation: Even multiplicity → the graph touches the x-axis but does not cross it. The sign of the factor stays the same on both sides of an even-multiplicity zero, producing the bounce.

quizQuestions.question: The polynomial f(x) = (x − 1)²(x + 3) has zeros at:
quizQuestions.explanation: Set each factor to zero: x − 1 = 0 → x = 1; x + 3 = 0 → x = −3. The exponent 2 gives x=1 multiplicity two, while x=−3 has multiplicity one.

quizQuestions.question: Which polynomial has odd degree and a negative leading coefficient?
quizQuestions.explanation: The leading term −3x⁵ has odd degree and a negative coefficient, so the graph rises left and falls right.

quizQuestions.question: According to the Remainder Theorem, if p(x) is divided by (x − c), the remainder equals:
quizQuestions.explanation: The Remainder Theorem: dividing p(x) by (x − c) gives remainder p(c). Evaluating p at the divisor’s zero therefore finds the remainder without performing the full division.

quizQuestions.question: When x³ + 3x² − x − 3 is divided by (x − 1), which quotient results?
quizQuestions.explanation: Coefficients: 1, 3, −1, −3. Divide by 1: bring 1 down. 1+3=4, 4·1=4; −1+4=3, 3·1=3; −3+3=0. Quotient: x² + 4x + 3.

quizQuestions.question: The Factor Theorem states that (x − c) is a factor of p(x) if and only if:
quizQuestions.explanation: By the Factor Theorem, (x − c) is a factor exactly when p(c) = 0. A zero remainder is exactly what allows p(x) to be written as (x−c) times another polynomial.

quizQuestions.question: If p(2)=−5, what is the remainder when p(x) is divided by x−2?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Remainder Theorem says division by x−2 leaves the remainder p(2), which is −5.

quizQuestions.question: Divide x³−4x²+x+6 by x−2. What is the quotient?
quizQuestions.explanation: Synthetic division with 2 gives coefficients 1, −2, −3 and remainder 0, so the quotient is x²−2x−3.

quizQuestions.question: To simplify a rational expression, you factor the numerator and denominator and then:
options: Set the expression equal to zero
quizQuestions.explanation: Cancelling common factors in numerator and denominator simplifies the rational expression.

quizQuestions.question: Simplify: (2x² − 8)/(x − 2).
quizQuestions.explanation: 2x² − 8 = 2(x² − 4) = 2(x+2)(x−2). Divide by (x−2): 2(x+2). The cancellation is valid only when x≠2, the value excluded by the original denominator.

quizQuestions.question: What is the vertical asymptote of f(x) = 3/(x + 5)?
quizQuestions.explanation: Vertical asymptotes occur where the denominator is zero: x + 5 = 0 → x = −5.

quizQuestions.question: Solve 1/x + 1/3 = 5/6, noting any excluded value of x.
quizQuestions.explanation: Multiply through by 6x: 6 + 2x = 5x → 6 = 3x → x = 2. The solution is valid because x=2 is not excluded from either original denominator.

quizQuestions.question: What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=(3x²+1)/(x²−4)?
quizQuestions.explanation: Equal degrees give the ratio of leading coefficients, 3/1=3. Comparing leading terms also shows why lower-degree terms do not change this end-behavior ratio.

quizQuestions.question: Which values must be excluded from the domain of (x+2)/(x²−9)?
quizQuestions.explanation: The denominator factors as (x−3)(x+3), so both values make the original expression undefined.

quizQuestions.question: Simplify √(72a⁴) for real a.
quizQuestions.explanation: Because a² is nonnegative, √(72a⁴)=√(36·2)·√((a²)²)=6a²√2. No absolute value is needed on a² because a² is nonnegative for every real a.

quizQuestions.question: Rewrite x^(2/3) in radical form.
quizQuestions.explanation: x^(m/n) = ⁿ√(xᵐ). So x^(2/3) = ³√(x²). The denominator 3 becomes the root index, and the numerator 2 remains the exponent inside the radical.

quizQuestions.question: Solve √(x + 5) = 3 and verify the solution in the original equation.
quizQuestions.explanation: Square both sides: x + 5 = 9 → x = 4. Check: √(4+5) = √9 = 3 ✓. Checking in the original radical equation confirms that squaring did not introduce an extraneous solution.

quizQuestions.question: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x − 4)?
quizQuestions.explanation: The expression under a square root must be ≥ 0: x − 4 ≥ 0 → x ≥ 4. The endpoint x=4 is included because it makes the radicand zero, which has a real square root.

quizQuestions.question: Which is an extraneous solution of √(2x − 1) = x − 2?
quizQuestions.explanation: Squaring gives 2x − 1 = x² − 4x + 4 → x² − 6x + 5 = 0 → x = 1 or x = 5. Check x = 1: √1 = 1 but x − 2 = −1. Extraneous.

quizQuestions.question: For real x, simplify √(50x²).
quizQuestions.explanation: √(50x²) = √(25 · 2 · x²) = 5|x|√2 for real x. The absolute value is required because √(x²)=|x| for real x.

quizQuestions.question: The function f(x) = 3^x represents:
quizQuestions.explanation: A base greater than 1 gives exponential growth. For an exponential function b^x, bases above 1 increase as x increases; bases between 0 and 1 decay.

quizQuestions.question: What is the y-intercept of f(x) = 5 · 2^x?
quizQuestions.explanation: f(0) = 5 · 2⁰ = 5 · 1 = 5. y-intercept is (0, 5). The coefficient 5 is the initial value because the exponential factor equals 1 at x=0.

quizQuestions.question: $500 is invested at 6% compounded annually. What is the amount after 2 years?
quizQuestions.explanation: A = 500(1 + 0.06)² = 500(1.06)² = 500(1.1236) = $561.80. The annual compounding uses two growth factors of 1.06, not simple interest added twice.

quizQuestions.question: Which function represents exponential decay with an initial value of 12?
quizQuestions.explanation: The coefficient 12 is the initial value and the base 0.8 lies between 0 and 1, so the model decays exponentially.

quizQuestions.question: What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=2^x+3?
quizQuestions.explanation: The graph of 2^x has asymptote y=0; shifting it up 3 units gives y=3. The added constant changes every output by 3, so the graph approaches 3 as x decreases without reaching it.

quizQuestions.question: Which function is exponential decay and has initial value 1?
quizQuestions.explanation: Its base lies between 0 and 1, so it decays, and f(0)=1. The other choices either grow or have an initial value different from 1, so they fail one of the two stated conditions.

quizQuestions.question: Use the corresponding exponential equation to evaluate log₅(125).
quizQuestions.explanation: 5³ = 125, so log₅(125) = 3. The logarithm asks for the exponent on 5 that produces 125.

quizQuestions.question: Which property states log(xⁿ) = n·log(x)?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Power Rule of logarithms: log(xⁿ) = n · log(x). The exponent moves in front as a multiplier; it does not create a product or quotient inside the logarithm.

quizQuestions.question: For x>0, use a logarithm property to expand log₂(8x).
quizQuestions.explanation: Product rule: log₂(8x) = log₂(8) + log₂(x) = 3 + log₂(x). Since log₂(8)=3, the expansion can also be written 3+log₂(x), with x>0.

quizQuestions.question: A student rewrites log₂(x−1)=3 in exponential form. Which value of x satisfies the equation and its domain?
quizQuestions.explanation: Rewrite as x−1=2³=8, giving x=9, which satisfies the domain condition x>1. The domain check rules out any value at or below 1 before accepting the algebraic result.

quizQuestions.question: Solve log(x)+log(x+3)=1, where log means base 10.
quizQuestions.explanation: Combining logs gives x(x+3)=10. The roots are 2 and −5, but only 2 satisfies both log domains.

quizQuestions.question: After two Carbon-14 half-lives, or 11,460 years, what fraction of the original amount remains?
quizQuestions.explanation: 11,460 years = 2 half-lives. After 2 half-lives: (1/2)² = 1/4 of original remains.

quizQuestions.question: A substance with [H⁺] = 0.001 mol/L has pH =:
quizQuestions.explanation: pH = −log(0.001) = −log(10⁻³) = 3. Because 0.001=10⁻³, taking the negative base-10 logarithm changes −3 to 3.

quizQuestions.question: An earthquake measures 7.0 on the Richter scale. Another measures 5.0. The first is how many times more intense?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Richter scale is logarithmic: difference of 2 means 10² = 100 times more intense.

quizQuestions.question: A population grows continuously at 4% per year. Starting with 1,000, the model is:
quizQuestions.explanation: Continuous growth uses A = Pe^(rt) where r = 0.04. The coefficient 1000 is the initial population and the positive exponent gives continuous growth.

quizQuestions.question: If a quantity follows A(t)=600e^(−0.2t), which statement describes its continuous rate?
options: It decays continuously at 20% per time unit
It grows continuously at 20% per time unit
It decays by exactly 20 units per time unit
quizQuestions.answer: It decays continuously at 20% per time unit
quizQuestions.explanation: In A=A₀e^(rt), r=−0.2. The negative exponent gives continuous decay and A₀=600 is the initial amount.

quizQuestions.question: Find the common difference of the sequence: 5, 9, 13, 17, …
quizQuestions.explanation: d = 9 − 5 = 4. Verify: 13 − 9 = 4. ✓. A constant difference between every pair of consecutive terms identifies an arithmetic sequence.

quizQuestions.question: Find the common ratio of the geometric sequence: 2, 6, 18, 54, …
quizQuestions.explanation: r = 6/2 = 3. Verify: 18/6 = 3. ✓. A constant quotient between consecutive nonzero terms identifies a geometric sequence.

quizQuestions.question: Evaluate: Σ(k=1 to 4) of 3k.
quizQuestions.explanation: 3(1) + 3(2) + 3(3) + 3(4) = 3 + 6 + 9 + 12 = 30. The sigma notation includes four terms, so each integer from 1 through 4 must be substituted.

quizQuestions.question: What is the explicit formula for the arithmetic sequence 5, 9, 13, 17, …?
quizQuestions.explanation: An arithmetic sequence uses aₙ=a₁+d(n−1); here a₁=5 and d=4. Substituting n=1 returns 5, and increasing n by 1 adds the common difference 4.

quizQuestions.question: Which infinite geometric series converges?
quizQuestions.explanation: An infinite geometric series converges only when |r|<1. The first series has r=1/2; the others have |r|≥1.

quizQuestions.question: Which conic section is represented by x² + y² = 25?
quizQuestions.explanation: x² + y² = r² is the standard form of a circle centered at the origin with radius r = 5.

quizQuestions.question: What are the foci of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/16 = 1?
quizQuestions.explanation: c² = a² − b² = 25 − 16 = 9 → c = 3. Foci: (±3, 0) along horizontal major axis.

quizQuestions.question: Which direction does the parabola y² = 8x open?
quizQuestions.explanation: Parabola of form y² = 4px opens right when p > 0. Here 4p = 8 so p = 2 > 0.

quizQuestions.question: What are the asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1?
quizQuestions.explanation: Asymptotes of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 are y = ±(b/a)x. Here b = 4, a = 3. y = ±(4/3)x.

quizQuestions.question: For (x−2)²+(y+3)²=16, what are the center and radius?
quizQuestions.explanation: The form (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r² gives h=2, k=−3, and r=4. The signs inside each square reverse the coordinate signs, while the right side gives r²=16.

quizQuestions.question: A restaurant offers 3 appetizers, 5 entrees, and 2 desserts. How many different meals (one of each) are possible?
quizQuestions.explanation: Fundamental Counting Principle: 3 × 5 × 2 = 30. The choices are independent, so multiplying the three counts includes every appetizer–entrée–dessert combination once.

quizQuestions.question: How many ways can 4 students be arranged in a line from a group of 10?
quizQuestions.explanation: P(10, 4) = 10!/(10−4)! = 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040. Order matters in a line, so this is a permutation rather than a combination.

quizQuestions.question: How many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
quizQuestions.explanation: C(8, 3) = 8!/(3! · 5!) = (8 × 7 × 6)/(3 × 2 × 1) = 336/6 = 56. Order does not matter for committee membership, so the combination formula divides out the 3! arrangements.

quizQuestions.question: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue marbles. What is the probability of drawing a red marble?
quizQuestions.explanation: P(red) = 4/(4+6) = 4/10 = 2/5. There are ten equally likely marbles in total, four of which satisfy the event.

quizQuestions.question: Two dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
A card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. Given that it is a face card, what is the probability it is a queen?
quizQuestions.explanation: There are 12 face cards and 4 queens, so P(queen | face card)=4/12=1/3. Conditioning restricts the sample space to the 12 face cards before counting the four queens.

quizQuestions.question: In a data set with an extreme outlier, which measure of center is usually pulled the most?
quizQuestions.explanation: The mean uses all data values and is sensitive to extreme values (outliers).

quizQuestions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately what percent of data falls within one standard deviation of the mean?
quizQuestions.explanation: The empirical (68-95-99.7) rule: approximately 68% falls within ±1σ of the mean.

quizQuestions.question: A data set has mean 50 and standard deviation 10. What z-score corresponds to a value of 35?
quizQuestions.explanation: z = (35 − 50)/10 = −15/10 = −1.5. The negative sign shows 35 is below the mean, while 1.5 gives the distance in standard deviations.

quizQuestions.question: A value has z=−1.8. How should it be interpreted?
options: It is 1.8 standard deviations below the mean
It is 1.8 standard deviations above the mean
quizQuestions.answer: It is 1.8 standard deviations below the mean
quizQuestions.explanation: A negative z-score places the value below the mean, and its magnitude gives the distance in standard deviations.

quizQuestions.question: For a normal distribution with mean 100 and standard deviation 15, about what percent lies from 70 to 130?
quizQuestions.explanation: The interval is μ±2σ, so the empirical rule gives about 95%. Here 70 and 130 are exactly two standard deviations below and above the mean: 100±2(15).

quizQuestions.question: What is the size of the product of a 2×3 matrix and a 3×4 matrix?
quizQuestions.explanation: Matrix product of m×n and n×p gives an m×p matrix. 2×3 · 3×4 = 2×4. The matching inner dimensions 3 confirm multiplication is defined, and the outer dimensions give the product size.

quizQuestions.question: What is the determinant of the matrix [[3, 1], [2, 4]]?
quizQuestions.explanation: det = 3·4 − 1·2 = 12 − 2 = 10. For a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], the determinant is ad−bc.

quizQuestions.question: Two matrices A and B can be added if and only if they:
options: Have the same size (same rows and columns)
quizQuestions.answer: Have the same size (same rows and columns)
quizQuestions.explanation: Matrix addition is defined only for matrices with identical dimensions. Matching determinants or being square does not make entry-by-entry addition valid when dimensions differ.

quizQuestions.question: If A=[[1,2],[3,4]] and B=[[2],[5]], what is the first entry of AB?
quizQuestions.explanation: The first entry is the dot product of A’s first row and B’s column: 1·2+2·5=12.

quizQuestions.question: If AX=B and A is invertible, which expression equals X?
quizQuestions.explanation: Left-multiply by A⁻¹ to obtain X=A⁻¹B. Matrix order matters: multiplying on the left preserves A⁻¹A=I and leaves X on the left side.

quizQuestions.question: When a three-equation system in x, y, and z has a unique solution, that solution is represented by:
quizQuestions.explanation: A unique solution assigns one value to each variable, forming an ordered triple. Other systems may have no solution or infinitely many solutions.

quizQuestions.question: If a bounded feasible region has a maximum value for a linear objective, where can at least one maximum be found?
options: At a vertex of the feasible region
quizQuestions.answer: At a vertex of the feasible region
quizQuestions.explanation: A linear objective over a bounded polygon attains a maximum at one or more vertices, though an entire edge can tie when the objective is parallel to that edge.

quizQuestions.question: Which ordered triple satisfies the system: x + y + z = 6, x − y = 1, z = 2?
Which region is the solution to the system: y ≤ 2x + 1 and y ≥ −x + 3?
options: To the right of both lines
quizQuestions.explanation: The solution is where y is both ≤ 2x+1 (below the first line) and ≥ −x+3 (above the second line) — the region between them.

quizQuestions.question: For the feasible vertices (0,0), (0,4), and (2,4), where is P=3x+2y largest?
quizQuestions.explanation: Evaluate the linear objective at each vertex: 0, 8, and 14. The greatest value is 14 at (2,4).
